message.content: {"caption":"A three-stage knowledge-incorporation workflow shows a passage being converted into a self-edit, used for an SFT update, and evaluated by answering a question about the passage.","description":"Diagram titled “Knowledge Incorporation Setup,” arranged left to right in three panels: “Passage,” “Self-Edit,” and “Evaluation.” In Passage, the text reads “title: Apollo program” and “context: But even after NASA reached internal agreement, it was far from smooth sailing...” with a blue underline beneath the passage. A right-pointing arrow leads to a model block labeled “LM” with a coral parameter tile θₜ, then another right-pointing arrow leads to Self-Edit. The self-edit text is “1. The Apollo program faced opposition from Kennedy’s science advisor, Jerome Wiesner, who had...” and has a yellow underline. A right-pointing arrow leads to a lavender “SFT” block. Above it is a coral tile labeled θₜ′, connected to the SFT block by an upward-pointing arrow. A vertical divider separates Evaluation. Its question reads “Who was Kennedy’s science adviser that opposed manned spacecraft flights?” with a blue underline. A right-pointing arrow leads to an “LM” block containing a coral θₜ′ tile, followed by another right-pointing arrow to the answer “Jerome Wiesner”; a check mark above the answer indicates it is marked correct.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
